name: Conductor branching from a group
summary: One conductor drawn leaving a single-line conductor group at an angle, showing where it splits from the bundle.
description: When conductors are drawn as a single line or bundle, a breakout shows the point where one conductor leaves the group to go elsewhere. The leaving conductor is normally drawn at an angle or with a short curve and carries its own identifier, so that the group line beyond the breakout has one less conductor.

The breakout is a drawing convention, not a physical joint. No splice or terminal exists at the point unless a separate symbol is placed there. Readers should track the conductor count on each side of the breakout and confirm the identifiers match on both.
readingNotes: Track conductor count either side of the breakout.
Do not read the breakout as a splice.
drawingChecklist: Label the conductor that leaves the group.
Update the count on the remaining group line.
Add a splice symbol only where a physical joint exists.
distinction: A breakout is a drawing convention for a conductor leaving a bundle; a wire splice is a physical joint.
